data.name: Mad Crown
data.detailed_description:
Mad Crown is a roguelike RPG set in a post-apocalyptic dieselpunk world. As an explorer, you are in search of the legendary crown. Make use of limited resources and meticulous tactics to battle an eerie enemy through the procedurally generated dungeons of a mutated world.



World Settings
Mad Crown is a dungeon crawling roguelike RPG set in a dieselpunk world set hundreds of years after the human race destroyed the world with nuclear weapons. The nuclear Armageddon awoke god like leviathans from beneath the earth’s surface and a doomsday battle between these creatures devastated the planet's surface. Now a hundred years after the fabled battle of the gods, Humans try to carve out an existence in the mutated land filled with repulsive creatures.
Rumors have surfaced about the existence of the Mad Crown. A powerful artifact said to hold untold power that would rival the gods. Thus, you, like many others before have set out to find the Mad Crown .



Game Features
  • Roguelike elements: Initial level zero setting, penalties for player death, inventory management, survival mechanics.
  • Procedurally generated dungeons.
  • Tough boss battles.
  • In-depth tactical turn-based combat.
  • Card deck system: use items and ability cards inside and outside of combat to your tactical advantage.
  • Vivid art style and scored soundtrack.
  • Adventurers reciprocal rescue! Adventurers can work together to rescue one another
    • If you die other adventurers can reach out to and help retrieve all lost items
    • Join a rescue team to help other adventurers killed in the Ruins and win respect and rewards
  • Witty monster character mechanics.
  • Large enemy variety with multiple strategies.
  • 10 available characters classes.
  • Over 200 items to suit your party.
  • Challenging levels and special modes

reviews.review:
Mad Crown has decent music and good, quirky artdesign. But those are the only two good hairs I can leave on the game.

For Gameplay, it's like somebody looked at all the worst parts of Darkest Dungeon and ported them into a whole new game.

Firstly, theres Hitchances. On mylast run I actually payed special attention to how many times my party actually hit versus missed their attacks. And the score threatened to break even a couple of times. This means that on a very basic level, combat difficulty is not governed by tactical choices or preparation, but more if the game is in the "mood" to let you actually connect attacks. I'm not saying that a very low-threat kind of combat system CANT work, but enemies hit their attacks just fine, and theres a certain mechanic that makes missing way more of a downside to the player than the AI.

If a Monster kills another Monsters, it upgrades itself by 5 Levels. From me mentioning this you can probably guess that there are certain scenarios where there's friendly fire. This would be a cute gimmick in most cases, but in Mad Crown it can mount to a lost run due to randomness. Say you beat an enemy to a sliver of health, and then proceed to miss EVERY attack afterwards on it. Eventually it'll get murdered by it's mates. If this happens once, it makes combat harder and will cost you more life and stamina. If it happens twice, you're boned unless you happen to have poison runes stocked (Since they deal percentages, and thus will kill lvl 100 Godzilla just as fast as Level 1 Godzilla). If it happens thrice (Yes, totally a thing), you can kiss your run goodbye.

Even beyond that, tactical choices are minimal. Every hero has 3 abilities and a passive. Can't level them up, cant customize them beyond what equipment you slap onto them. Which comes down to getting the best numbers, and not much else. What I think the game is TRYING to do, is balance the stack by providing the player with Inscriptions, or runes, or whatever you want to call them. They are one-use items that can be deployed in combat, to revive fallen heros, inflict enemies with statutes or even just straight damage them with an element. But here too, what you get and when is entirely random, and thus your ability to take advantage is minimal.

The crawling itself isnt doing the player any favours either. Traps are invisible until stepped on and will damage or inflict statues. Theres a fog of war which can make entirely impossible to tell where mosnter groups lurk, so theres no avoiding them either. There's random curse effects which afflict item in your packs, making them unuseable.

THe game sort of lures you in with it's quirky design and decent music, but makes it perfectly clear that it hates the player and doesnt want him to suceed or get anything. "No you take damage now." "No you're posioned now." "You now miss 5 times in a row." It isn't fun or interesting, it's random and a chore.

I realize this is harsh, but you can just tell nobody really put any thought into making Mad Crown an interesting challenge. Maybe they got tired of trying halfway trough and just started adding random qualifiers to everything.

I'm not gonna hold the barebones translation against the game, since it was basically only given out so you could "take a look". Def. dont go into this if you cant handle a little bit of engrish. But even if you can, honestly not worth the money. Darkest Dungeon does almost everything Mad Crown does, and better to boot. Stay away, at least until EA's over and we can see what the Dev tries to fix.
reviews.developer_response:
Thanks for your valuable feedback!

Most design issues mentioned is also feedbacked from other players as well, that's also the point of early-access period. But it takes time for us to develop and carry out any improvements, and we will have them fixed later.

In the following updates, we will focus on pre-battle options and tactics, to let players have more options against challenges.

As for the randomness, since it is the essential part of our gameplay, we plan not to make our game more calculation-based, like Darkest Dungeon does. However it is understandable that randomness can lead to over-frustration in our game so we will try our best to figure out a solution to fix it.
